title: Answer: no account of intelligence, only the cognitive tasks that need the workspace

statements.text: The global workspace theory takes no position on what intelligence is. What it says nearby is which cognitive tasks need consciousness: those that require holding information for a long time, novel combinations of operations, or intentional behavior that starts spontaneously. Much other processing runs without consciousness in modular networks working in parallel.
statements.scope: the 2001 workspace framework of Dehaene and Naccache

sources.quote: including those that require durable information maintenance, novel combinations of operations, or the spontaneous generation of intentional behavior.
many modular cerebral networks are active in parallel and process information in an unconscious manner.
